rachel: Partner reported duplicate side-effect when a 429 hit right as the client started a token refresh. Logs show immediate retry succeeded then queued drain also succeeded. :(

sam: ouch. can you paste a tiny sanitized log?

rachel: snippet:
```
2025-09-12T12:15:00Z req id=abc status=429 retry-after=0.3
2025-09-12T12:15:00Z auth refresh start
2025-09-12T12:15:00Z internal retry -> 200 (applied)
2025-09-12T12:15:01Z auth refresh done; drained queue -> 200 (applied)
```

yves: clear race. proposal: make SDKs "hold" (enqueue) mutating requests while auth refresh is in-flight by default. If request includes an explicit Idempotency-Key allow immediate send (server dedupe). Always honor Retry-After if present.

sam: defense-in-depth: add short in-memory fingerprint dedupe (method+path+body hash) with TTL ~8000ms and small LRU (default 2000 entries) to skip re-sends when servers don't support idempotency.

yves: jitter/backoff for 429 immediate retries (when allowed): delay = base * (2 ** attempt) * (0.75 + Math.random() * 0.5) capped at 2500ms.

sam: parity: Node currently mixed; Py behaves differently in places. We'll align defaults to "hold" across SDKs and expose config `replay_strategy = "hold" | "passthrough"`.

rachel: plan: sam -> Node SDK queueing + fingerprint cache + telemetry metric sdk.replay.during_refresh.count; yves -> sampleapp add Idempotency-Key examples and e2e test; I'll do partner comms and docs.

qa-bot: CI queued: run/tests (node-sdk) #4001 by sam

rachel: timeline: aim to ship Node patch next week, Py parity following sprint. I'll open RFC and drop link here. :thumbsup:
